questions.question: What does a compiler actually do?
options: It turns the text you wrote into instructions the machine can run
It runs your program one line at a time as you type
It checks your program against the internet for mistakes
It makes your program faster by rewriting your logic
questions.explanation: A compiler reads your source text and produces a runnable program, or refuses and reports why. It never guesses what you meant.

questions.question: In int battery_percent(int millivolts), what does the leading int describe?
options: The type of value the function hands back
The number of arguments the function takes
The amount of memory the function is allowed to use
That the function can only be called with whole numbers
questions.explanation: The type written before the function name is the type of its return value. The parameter types are the ones inside the parentheses.

questions.question: Why does the worked solution handle 3000 and 4200 before doing any arithmetic?
options: So the rest of the function can never produce a value outside 0 to 100
Because arithmetic is slower than comparison
Because C++ requires every function to start with an if statement
To avoid dividing by zero
questions.explanation: Clamping the ends first means the remaining code only ever deals with readings inside the range, so it cannot produce an out of range answer.

questions.question: A reading of 3600 millivolts should report what percentage?
options: 50, because it sits exactly halfway between 3000 and 4200
36, because the reading is 3600
86, because 3600 divided by 4200 is about 0.86
0, because it is below the full voltage
questions.explanation: The range runs from 3000 to 4200, which is 1200 wide. A reading of 3600 is 600 above empty, exactly half of 1200.

questions.question: Your program compiles and runs but reports the wrong percentage. What does that tell you?
options: The compiler accepted what you wrote, and what you wrote is not what you meant
The compiler is broken and should be reinstalled
The test file must be wrong
The program needs to be run with administrator permissions
questions.explanation: A compiler checks whether your text is valid C++, not whether your logic is correct. Tests are what check the second thing.

questions.question: Why does production firmware usually not use a straight line for battery percentage?
options: A lithium cell does not discharge evenly, so a straight line misreports the middle
Straight lines are too slow to compute on a microcontroller
Percentages are not allowed in safety critical code
The compiler cannot optimise division by a constant
questions.explanation: Real cells have a discharge curve, so firmware uses a measured lookup table or counts charge in and out. The straight line is still an honest first answer.
